record.original_question: Let G be a semisimple real algebraic group, Γ a noncocompact arithmetic lattice, and D a closed subgroup of a maximal R-split torus A. Are there no divergent D-orbits when dim D>rank_Q G, are all divergent trajectories obvious when dim D=rank_Q G, and do non-obvious divergent trajectories exist when dim D<rank_Q G?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 25 (Barak Weiss). 1. If dim D > rankQG, then there are no diver-gent orbits of D. 2. If dim D = rankQG, then the only divergent trajectories are obvious ones. 3. If dim D < rankQG, then there are non-obvious divergent trajectories.

artifact.category_tag: Divergent torus orbits in homogeneous spaces
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a semisimple real algebraic group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a noncocompact arithmetic lattice, and let $A \subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split torus. Let $D \subset A$ be a closed subgroup. A trajectory $\{d \cdot x\Gamma : d \in D\}$ in $G/\Gamma$ is called divergent if the map $D \to G/\Gamma$, $d \mapsto d \cdot x\Gamma$, is proper (i.e. the orbit eventually leaves every compact subset of $G/\Gamma$). A divergent trajectory is called obvious if its divergence can be detected from a finite collection of algebraic ($\mathbb{Q}$-rational) data, namely from the divergence in $\mathbb{R}$ of evaluations of $\mathbb{Q}$-characters of suitable $\mathbb{Q}$-parabolic subgroups along the orbit. Let $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$ denote the $\mathbb{Q}$-rank of $G$. Establish the following three statements:

(1) If $\dim D > \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then there are no divergent $D$-orbits in $G/\Gamma$.

(2) If $\dim D = \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then every divergent $D$-trajectory in $G/\Gamma$ is obvious.

(3) If $\dim D < \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then there exist non-obvious divergent $D$-trajectories in $G/\Gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The three-part conjecture has been partially resolved. Part (1) was established by Weiss, showing that any diagonalizable subgroup admitting a divergent trajectory has dimension at most $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$. Part (3) (existence of non-obvious divergent trajectories when $\dim D < \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$) has been established in a modified form via work proving non-obvious divergent trajectories under dimension constraints relative to $\mathbb{Q}$-factors. Part (2) (classification of divergent trajectories as obvious when $\dim D = \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$) is known in $\mathbb{Q}$-rank two (Tomanov–Weiss, and rank-two arithmetic homogeneous spaces) but the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Divergent trajectories and Q-rank
status_evidence.snippet: If A admits a divergent trajectory in G/Γ then dim A ≤ rank_Q G.
status_evidence.claim: Part (1) of the conjecture is established.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Non-Obvious Divergent Trajectories in homogeneous spaces
status_evidence.snippet: A modified version of a conjecture of Weiss from 2004 was proven... if the projection of A to any Q-factor of G is of small enough dimension, there are non-obvious divergent trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Part (3) has been verified in a modified form.

status_evidence.title: Divergent trajectories in arithmetic homogeneous spaces of rational rank two
status_evidence.snippet: Full classification under rank_Q G = rank_R G = 2.

status_evidence.title: Closed orbits for actions of maximal tori on homogeneous spaces (Tomanov–Weiss)
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic description of closed/divergent torus orbits.
